meta.title: Md. Mahmudul Islam | Project Management | Telecom Digital Delivery
meta.description: Program Management Manager at Banglalink Digital Communications (VEON Group). Ten years delivering telecom, logistics and e-governance programmes under PMO governance.

tagline.normal: I turn ambiguous projects into dated, measurable go-lives.
tagline.zb: Committees talk. I ship. Ten years of go-lives that actually went live.

programmes.name: Nationwide door-to-door fulfilment for Banglalink

body.normal: One platform consolidating SIM services, FWA, MNP, transfer of ownership and device ordering with automated rider assignment behind it. I ran delivery governance across product, IT, commercial and field operations, from UAT sign-off through to launch.
body.zb: Five separate services crammed into one platform, launched nationwide without slipping the date. Product, IT, commercial and field ops all pulling in different directions; my job was making them pull in one.

programmes.result: Same-day fulfilment for orders placed before noon, across all 64 districts.

programmes.name: EkPay | Bangladesh's centralized P2G bill payment platform or A2i

body.normal: EkPay is Bangladesh's largest payment aggregator — the A2i initiative to give citizens a single centralized People-to-Government payment platform under the Digital Bangladesh vision. I worked on delivery of a platform connecting 15+ banks, 30+ service providers, 50+ assisted agents and 50,000+ syndicated agents, letting citizens pay any bill from cards, bank accounts or digital credit in one place.
body.zb: Before EkPay: a citizen queued at one office to pay one bill, then queued at another. After: one platform, 15+ banks, 30+ service providers, 50,000+ agents — every government bill payable from a phone. That's what 'Digital Bangladesh' looks like when it ships instead of staying a slogan.

programmes.result: One centralized platform for citizen-to-government payments, spanning 15+ banks and 50,000+ agents nationwide.

programmes.name: MVNO partnership — scope, journeys and regulatory path

body.normal: Built the business scope for a state-operator MVNO partnership: cross-operator after-sales routing, the number-portability journey, and a customer onboarding flow with regulatory validation designed in from the start rather than bolted on afterwards.
body.zb: Regulatory sign-off is where partnerships go to die, so I designed it into the onboarding flow on day one instead of praying for it at the end.

programmes.result: Regulatory checkpoints embedded directly in the onboarding flow.

board.head: How the sausage gets made
board.hint: Drag the post-its. Click a cell — it pops, it falls. Nothing here is permanent, which is rather the point.

body.normal: PMO structures that survive contact with reality. RAID discipline, gate criteria agreed before the gate, and status that still reports the truth on a bad week.
body.zb: Status reports that stay honest on bad weeks. If your RAG is always green, someone is lying to you.

body.normal: Operational flows mapped and rebuilt against eTOM, so the redesign is auditable against a standard instead of one team's preference.
body.zb: Rebuilt against eTOM, not against whoever shouted loudest in the workshop.

body.normal: CEO and ExCo material that leads with the decision needed. One slide, the ask visible, the supporting data one layer down.
body.zb: One slide. The ask at the top. Nobody has ever needed slide 34.
